Infinitesimal Jackknife Influence for an N-Mixture Model

Source: R/nmix.R
ijk_nmix.Rd

Computes site-level and observation (visit)-level influence values, i.e. posterior covariances between the quantity of interest and the log-likelihood components returned by nmix_loglik(). These are used by ijk_bootstrap_2stage() for the two-stage (site and visit) bootstrap approximation.

Usage

ijk_nmix(theta, loglik, obs = c("rb", "joint"))

Arguments

theta

Finite numeric vector (length \(S\), with \(S \ge 2\)) of posterior draws of the quantity of interest, or a finite numeric \(S \times K\) matrix for \(K\) quantities at once (e.g. a regression curve on a grid). The number of rows must match loglik.

loglik

An object of class "nmix_loglik".

obs

Which observation-level log-likelihood to use: "rb" for quantities depending only on the parameters, "joint" for quantities that depend on the latent abundance \(N\).

Value

An object of class "ijk_nmix" containing

estimate

Posterior mean(s).

influence_site

Site-level influence values (centred, as in ijk()); a vector of length \(I\), or an \(I \times K\) matrix.

influence_obs

Observation-level influence values; length \(IJ\) (ordered \(i + (j-1)I\)), 0 for missing visits.

obs_mask

Observed-visit indicator.

obs

The obs argument.

The site-level influence can be passed to ijk_lko() for an approximate leave-one-site-out analysis.

Details

The first-order approximation of the posterior mean under site weights \(u_i\) and visit weights \(v_{ij}\) is $$E_{u,v}[\theta] \approx E[\theta] + \sum_i (u_i - 1) c_i + \sum_{i,j} (v_{ij} - 1) e_{ij},$$ with \(c_i = \mathrm{Cov}[\theta, \ell_i]\) (site-level marginal log-likelihood) and \(e_{ij} = \mathrm{Cov}[\theta, \ell_{ij}]\) (observation-level log-likelihood).

See also

nmix_loglik(), ijk_bootstrap_2stage()

Examples

set.seed(1)
I <- 10; J <- 3; S <- 200
y <- matrix(rpois(I * J, 3), I, J)
lambda <- matrix(rgamma(S * I, 20, 4), S, I)
p <- matrix(runif(S * I * J, 0.4, 0.7), S, I * J)
ll <- nmix_loglik(y, lambda, p)
fit <- ijk_nmix(rowSums(lambda), ll)
fit$estimate
#> [1] 49.89695
